skills.name: Scenario-to-Functional Attribute Grounding
skills.task_description: Convert a scenario-led shopping request into catalog-visible functional product attributes before retrieval.
skills.state_description: A request names a use occasion or outcome such as outdoor activity, travel, comfort, protection, or all-day use.
skills.solution_description: Keep the product type explicit, preserve the original scenario in the query, and promote only concrete functional cues that can distinguish catalog items.

thought_template.objective: Separate product type from use situation.
thought_template.guard: The user names a visible occasion or desired outcome.

thought_template.objective: Map visible functional language into required and preferred catalog terms.
thought_template.guard: Only public terms or their transparent lexical normalizations are used.

thought_template.objective: Retain scenario language when no reliable attribute conversion is available.
thought_template.guard: Catalog terminology is uncertain.

insights.trigger: The request describes a life situation rather than a spec sheet.
insights.principle: Scenario words carry preference evidence but should not erase the product type.
insights.intended_effect: Avoid generic category retrieval while remaining grounded in user language.

insights.principle: Use it as a preference term unless the user explicitly makes it non-negotiable.
insights.intended_effect: Prevent brittle over-filtering on imperfect Amazon metadata.

skills.provenance: Seeded from legacy TAIRA occasion-to-attribute planning and train-only development taxonomy.

skills.name: Audience, Fit, and Compatibility Grounding
skills.task_description: Translate visible demographic, size, body-fit, or compatibility language into high-priority catalog evidence.
skills.state_description: The request names an audience, life stage, body fit, or product compatibility that changes which items can be suitable.
skills.solution_description: Treat explicit audience and fit language as retention-critical evidence; use it to exclude incompatible taxonomy while allowing function and style to rank within the remaining pool.

thought_template.objective: Identify audience or fit assertions stated by the user.
thought_template.guard: An audience or compatibility cue is literally present.

thought_template.objective: Keep compatible taxonomy and fit cues in the retrieval frame.
thought_template.guard: The cue can be represented by title, category, or description terms.

insights.principle: Do not demote it merely because style or occasion terms are richer.
insights.intended_effect: Avoid superficially attractive but incompatible recommendations.

insights.trigger: Fit terms are absent from some catalog rows.
insights.principle: Prefer observable compatible evidence over inventing a fit judgment.

skills.provenance: Seeded from legacy TAIRA complex-intent fit and user-group query families.

skills.name: Multi-Occasion Branching and Shared-Core Search
skills.task_description: Plan retrieval for a request that spans multiple occasions or requirement bundles without collapsing their semantic distinction.
skills.state_description: The user names two or more use situations, style contexts, or performance requirements that may share a product core but differ in priority.
skills.solution_description: Retain common product requirements, expose the distinct occasion branches, and ask for a priority only when the branches cannot be reconciled by one public retrieval frame.

thought_template.objective: List the shared target and the distinct visible occasions.
thought_template.guard: More than one scenario or requirement is public.

thought_template.objective: Build a common retrieval frame before requesting extra dialogue.
thought_template.guard: The shared product type remains coherent.

thought_template.objective: Ask only for the branch that determines the recommendation.
thought_template.guard: Visible branches impose incompatible priorities.

insights.trigger: Two occasions appear in one request.
insights.principle: Multiple situations are not automatically a contradiction; first preserve their shared product core.
insights.intended_effect: Avoid needless questioning and preserve legacy multi-requirement planning.

insights.principle: Ask about the decision boundary rather than reciting all known constraints.

skills.provenance: Seeded from legacy TAIRA multi-occasion and differentiated-plan Thought Templates.

skills.name: Matching, Pairing, and Bundle Decomposition
skills.task_description: Handle pairing, matching, bundle, or multiple-target requests by separating the anchor need from supporting product roles.
skills.state_description: The request asks for compatible products, a coordinated set, or more than one product type.
skills.solution_description: Identify a primary recommendation target first; keep compatibility or supporting roles as retrieval preferences unless the user explicitly requires a complete bundle.

thought_template.objective: Determine the primary item role from explicit user language.
thought_template.guard: A compositional request contains multiple product roles.

thought_template.objective: Represent compatibility as a grounded preference for the anchor search.
thought_template.guard: The anchor product is known.

thought_template.objective: Clarify the primary recommendation role.
thought_template.guard: No principal product target is visible.

insights.trigger: The user asks for a coordinated outcome.
insights.principle: Do not flatten all roles into one vague query.
insights.intended_effect: Maintain the decomposition challenge of TAIRA's compositional intents.

insights.trigger: Only one item can be returned this turn.
insights.principle: Recommend the explicit anchor and explain the compatibility criterion rather than fabricating a full bundle.
insights.intended_effect: Keep execution honest under catalog constraints.

skills.provenance: Seeded from legacy TAIRA matching, pairing, bundle, and multiple-type query families.

skills.name: Taxonomy and Scenario Interpretation
skills.task_description: Resolve a visible ambiguity in audience, category, or use interpretation before committing to a narrow catalog search.
skills.state_description: The request admits two materially different public interpretations that lead to different product groups or constraints.
skills.solution_description: Name the smallest discriminating interpretation, ask once when needed, and keep the original wording intact for the next retrieval pass.

thought_template.objective: Identify the interpretation whose resolution changes the candidate pool.
thought_template.guard: At least two public readings are plausible.

thought_template.objective: Prepare a single concrete either-or or priority question.
thought_template.guard: The ambiguity cannot be resolved from visible text.

insights.trigger: The query contains an overloaded audience or occasion term.
insights.principle: Ask about the interpretation that changes catalog evidence, not a generic preference question.

skills.provenance: Seeded from legacy TAIRA ambiguous-scenario exploration patterns.

skills.name: Feedback-Priority Retrieval Rewrite
skills.task_description: Rewrite a prior catalog search when the user publicly elevates a previously secondary requirement.
skills.state_description: A prior recommendation has triggered an explicit correction, rejection, or priority update.
skills.solution_description: Retain the original target, promote the newly stated priority, exclude the shown slate, and do not reopen already settled questions.

thought_template.objective: Identify the correction stated after the prior slate.
thought_template.guard: The user visibly refers to a previous recommendation or unmet need.

thought_template.objective: Promote the new priority and exclude previously shown IDs.
thought_template.guard: At least one new public requirement is visible.

thought_template.objective: Ask only if the feedback cannot distinguish a repair route.
thought_template.guard: The correction is not actionable.

insights.trigger: A user says the prior option is close but changes priority.
insights.principle: Treat feedback as a reweighting signal, not a total reset.
insights.intended_effect: Preserve useful original intent while visibly repairing the failure.

insights.principle: Do not repeat its IDs unless the user explicitly asks to compare them.

skills.provenance: Seeded from legacy TAIRA failed-trajectory correction and new multi-turn revision traces.

skills.name: Verified Complex-Intent Direct Fulfillment
skills.task_description: Fulfill a sufficiently specified complex request without paying for an unnecessary dialogue turn.
skills.state_description: The visible request has a coherent target and enough public scenario or attribute evidence for a catalog-grounded recommendation.
skills.solution_description: Execute the matched semantic plan, rank a diverse Top-10 internal slate, and state the leading public evidence concisely.

thought_template.objective: Confirm the current retrieval frame has a coherent target.
thought_template.guard: DSUS marks the request recommendation-ready.

thought_template.objective: Produce a full-catalog Top-10 using the semantic Skill frame.
thought_template.guard: Only public catalog fields are used.

thought_template.objective: Recommend promptly with leading evidence.
thought_template.guard: The retrieved slate is non-empty.

insights.principle: A clarification has a real user cost; do not ask merely to make the state more detailed.
insights.intended_effect: Preserve efficiency on direct complex intents.

skills.provenance: State-conditioned extension of legacy TAIRA verified-intent fulfillment.

skills.name: Progressive Decisive-Constraint Elicitation
skills.task_description: Recover one missing decision-critical preference with the minimum possible interaction cost.
skills.state_description: The target is recognizable but one visible axis remains too underspecified to choose a trustworthy catalog route.
skills.solution_description: Ask a single unrepeated question that distinguishes plausible retrieval frames; after the answer, immediately rematch to fulfillment.

thought_template.objective: Choose the unresolved public axis with the highest candidate discrimination.
thought_template.guard: DSUS reports a missing decisive axis.

thought_template.objective: Ask one focused question in natural language.
thought_template.guard: The target has not already been asked.

thought_template.objective: Use the public answer to rematch a fulfillment Skill.
thought_template.guard: A user answer arrives.

insights.trigger: The request is broad but not incoherent.
insights.principle: Ask about the property that changes product suitability, not every missing catalog field.
insights.intended_effect: Create a useful clarification rather than an interview.

skills.provenance: State-conditioned extension of legacy TAIRA progressive elicitation experience.

skills.name: Ambiguous Interpretation Resolution
skills.task_description: Resolve one visible audience, category, or scenario ambiguity before committing to a product group.
skills.state_description: Two public interpretations would lead to materially different catalog evidence.
skills.solution_description: Ask a discriminating interpretation question, preserve both readings in memory, then recommend once the user selects or narrows one.

thought_template.objective: Name the two visible interpretations that change retrieval.
thought_template.guard: DSUS reports ambiguity.

thought_template.objective: Ask one concrete interpretation question.
thought_template.guard: The question has not been asked before.

thought_template.objective: Use the answer to route to semantic grounding and fulfillment.
thought_template.guard: A public answer arrives.

insights.trigger: There are two plausible product populations.
insights.principle: An explicit interpretation question is more valuable than a broad generic preference request.
insights.intended_effect: Avoid choosing the wrong product taxonomy with false confidence.

skills.provenance: State-conditioned extension of legacy TAIRA ambiguous scenario exploration.

skills.name: Visible Priority Conflict Negotiation
skills.task_description: Resolve a visible trade-off between requirements whose relative priority determines the recommendation.
skills.state_description: The user asks for potentially competing outcomes such as formal style plus travel comfort, or multiple incompatible audience/usage constraints.
skills.solution_description: Expose the single trade-off in user language, ask which outcome should dominate, and turn the answer into an explicit retrieval priority rather than silently dropping a requirement.

thought_template.objective: Identify the two visible requirements that cannot both dominate ranking.
thought_template.guard: DSUS reports conflict.

thought_template.objective: Ask which requirement should take precedence.
thought_template.guard: A priority has not already been supplied.

thought_template.objective: Promote the chosen priority in the retrieval frame.
thought_template.guard: A public priority answer arrives.

insights.trigger: The user states two attractive but competing goals.
insights.principle: Do not silently optimize one dimension and call it a match.
insights.intended_effect: Make conflict handling visible, explainable, and recoverable.

skills.provenance: Seeded from legacy TAIRA multi-requirement planning and new conflict transition design.

skills.name: Plausible-Option Probe and Comparative Feedback
skills.task_description: Offer an initially plausible catalog-grounded option when user feedback is likely to reveal the deciding priority more efficiently than a generic question.
skills.state_description: The visible request is broadly actionable but contains more than one reasonable ranking emphasis; a concrete option can elicit a correction.
skills.solution_description: Recommend a defensible leading option, retain the public slate, and treat any correction as a repair signal rather than a failed conversation.

thought_template.objective: Retrieve options satisfying the visible shared core.
thought_template.guard: The request is actionable but priority uncertainty remains.

thought_template.objective: Present a leading defensible option without pretending the priority is settled.
thought_template.guard: At least one public item is grounded.

thought_template.objective: Route feedback into the repair Skill.
thought_template.guard: The user reacts to the slate.

insights.principle: A concrete, relevant option can reveal a stable priority faster than an abstract question.
insights.intended_effect: Support revision-style interaction without using hidden labels.

skills.provenance: New multi-turn Skill derived from feedback-as-preference-evidence design.

skills.name: Feedback-Triggered Priority Repair
skills.task_description: Repair a recommendation when visible feedback promotes a new decision-critical priority.
skills.state_description: A prior recommendation is close or rejected, and the user has stated a concrete correction that can re-rank catalog candidates.
skills.solution_description: Use the feedback rewrite Skill, exclude the previous slate, and recommend a new grounded Top-10 without re-asking resolved preferences.

thought_template.objective: Verify that a new public priority is available for repair.
thought_template.guard: DSUS marks a revision or explicit rejection.

thought_template.objective: Re-rank using the revised frame and exclude shown IDs.
thought_template.guard: The revised frame has a visible target.

thought_template.objective: Give a repaired recommendation with concise evidence.
thought_template.guard: A new candidate slate exists.

thought_template.objective: Ask a targeted question only if feedback is non-actionable.
thought_template.guard: No repair frame can be built.

insights.trigger: Feedback contains a concrete priority shift.
insights.principle: Repair immediately; do not restart general elicitation.
insights.intended_effect: Reward the user for correcting the system and reduce abandonment risk.

skills.provenance: State-conditioned extension of legacy TAIRA failed-trajectory correction.

skills.name: Low-Patience Shortest Safe Path
skills.task_description: Avoid unnecessary interaction when public evidence already supports a safe recommendation or repair.
skills.state_description: The dialogue contains a usable frame and prior interaction has already consumed user attention.
skills.solution_description: Prefer one grounded recommendation over another generic question; reserve clarification for a clearly decision-changing unresolved axis.

thought_template.objective: Check whether another question would change the public retrieval frame.
thought_template.guard: At least one interaction has occurred.

thought_template.objective: Complete with a grounded slate when evidence is adequate.
thought_template.guard: The existing public frame is actionable.

insights.trigger: The user has already clarified or corrected the system.
insights.principle: Do not spend a second turn reconfirming the same decision boundary.
insights.intended_effect: Separate useful interaction from avoidable conversational cost.

skills.provenance: New efficiency Skill aligned with the frozen benchmark's path-sensitive evaluation.

skills.name: Dialogue Contract Reorientation
skills.task_description: Recover from an unhelpful visible branch without repeating the same question or recommendation.
skills.state_description: The user response makes clear that the previous interaction did not resolve the decision boundary, but no hidden information is assumed.
skills.solution_description: Switch to the smallest remaining public decision axis or safely stop; never manufacture a new preference or reuse a rejected slate.

thought_template.objective: Find a remaining public axis not already asked or shown.
thought_template.guard: A prior interaction did not resolve the visible need.

thought_template.objective: End gracefully when no grounded recovery action remains.
thought_template.guard: No new public evidence can justify another question or recommendation.

insights.principle: Recovery must be based on new public evidence, not a hidden simulation assumption.
insights.intended_effect: Keep re-planning auditable and prevent repetition loops.

skills.provenance: Seeded from legacy TAIRA corrected failures and public dialogue safety contracts.
